findings.issue: The wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a tree of this compilation. This includes location-less diagnostics (Location.None) for source-declared types, so existing diagnostics could be lost. That contradicts C4/C5/NF1/S1, and the fix is broader than the crash it addresses.

`FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()` yields a null location for metadata members. `Diagnostic.Create` with a null location makes a location-less diagnostic, and the constructor filter then silently drops it. The crash is swallowed instead of the metadata case being handled explicitly. Members of a type from metadata are also still processed and generated, which is inconsistent.

`GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null when the syntax is not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, not only for metadata. Examples are record primary-constructor parameter properties, which are source-declared, so those lose the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. The previous code would have thrown an InvalidCastException for them. This contradicts C10 and NF1.

The UnkeyedMember test locks in the silent dropping of the MsgPack004 diagnostic, and the test name and docs endorse it. Nothing tests that diagnostics for source-declared types are still reported, so NF1/S1 are unverified.

The doc claims an unattributed public member of a referenced type is reported by the defining project. That is not guaranteed. The defining project reports it only if it runs the analyzer, and a NuGet package or prebuilt DLL may not. The same over-claim appears in README.md line 1642 and in the code comment at TypeCollector.cs:1441.

The comment says the test fails on any diagnostic, but the test sets SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck. It also builds a separate manual compilation for the resolver check, which duplicates the setup and could drift from what the verifier actually runs.
